instruction.name: bcnez
instruction.description: Branch if condition code is non-zero (measured not taken).

throughput.name: 8 not-taken branches
throughput.asm: bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 0; movgr2cf $fcc0, $r4' --asm 'bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0; bcnez $fcc0, 0'

throughput.name: 8 taken branches, 32 static sites (fits in the BTB)
throughput.asm: bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 4 --unroll2 5 --iters 30000 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1; movgr2cf $fcc0, $r4' --asm 'bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4'
throughput.notes: Taken branches to the next instruction, 8 lanes x 4 static sites; the slope method compares the 8x4 body with 8x128, so at most 1024 branch sites. Fits in the LA464 BTB: 1 cycle per branch.

throughput.name: 8 taken branches, 960 static sites (exceeds the BTB)
throughput.asm: bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 120 --unroll2 128 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --init 'li.d $r4, 1; movgr2cf $fcc0, $r4' --asm 'bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4; bcnez $fcc0, 4'
throughput.notes: Taken branches to the next instruction, 8 lanes x 120 static sites; the slope method compares the 8x120 body with 8x128, so at most 1024 branch sites. Far beyond the LA464 BTB: about 3 cycles per branch.

notes: No destination data dependency; latency is not defined. Throughput only. Taken-branch throughput is recorded both for a footprint that fits in the BTB (1 CPI) and one that overflows it (~3 CPI).
